description.purpose: The container this member's assistants are instantiated into. It ships empty and open: no cells, no ports, no contract of its own. Its whole job is to be an address that already exists, so the mutation that instantiates an assistant has somewhere to put one -- and so the member can wire its holders and its CHANNELS to that address once instead of once per agent. Since GH #454 it is also where a turn is ADDRESSED: the channel stamps `context.assistant` with the name of the agent the person meant, and the per-assistant edges inside this container are what read it.
description.use_when: Never on its own -- it travels with member@1.5.0. Address it as <member>/assistants in the add_nodes of the mutation that instantiates an assistant, and draw that assistant's own edges in the same mutation. TRANSIT, derived from the contract of assistant@2.0.0 and from what this member sends back down (firewall@2.2.0, memory-hive@3.0.4) -- IN, three: the two a sibling of this container produces -- in_turn (the screened turn coming back from ./firewall on pass, carrying context.assistant) and in_bundle (the memory hive's answer) -- plus in_build_result, which enters at the member's own door and is forwarded here unchanged, because its producer sits four levels up. The four an assistant ALSO accepts -- in_advice, in_sweep, in_prune, in_round_sweep -- are deliberately NOT lanes of the member (ruling W7-R5): their producer is ./cogny inside the assistant, a second agent standing beside it in this container, or an operator or timer, and each of those addresses <member>/assistants/<agent> at its own path. That is allowed because neither this level nor the assistant declares params.ports, so both are open and the port boundary refuses an outside endpoint only for a SEALED hive. A lane a level declares but nothing ever crosses it on is the mirror image of one it emits with no edge -- see templates/member/README.md. OUT, the eight an assistant emits: answer, write, turn_write, extraction, recall, prune, error, build. Four of them stop at this level -- answer at ./channels, recall and extraction at ./memory-hive, write additionally fanned onto ./memory-hive's close pass -- and extraction is the one that must not stop HERE, in the container: it is the write half of the member's memory (GH #122, ADR 0012), wired the way talky's own recipe prescribes, two edges and never one. The others are re-emitted by the member on its own contract and leave the level; the parent drains them. ADDRESSING is the one thing this container costs per assistant: two edges, `./assistants -> ./assistants/<name>` on `in_turn` guarded on `context.assistant == '<name>'`, and `./assistants/<name> -> ./assistants` for each lane that leaves. The substrate resolves an edge target statically, so there is no way to write 'send it to whatever context.assistant names' as one edge -- a new assistant is a new pair of edges, and that is a rule rather than an accident. TWO of those lanes end DEEPER than the assistant since GH #562: the recall road is a v-lane (ADR-0020). `recall` leaves `./assistants/<name>/talky` and `./assistants/<name>/cogny` directly for this container's rim, carrying the `recall_caller` stamp, and `in_bundle` goes straight back down to the asker the token names -- four edges per assistant instead of the two that used to end at the generation's own path, each naming its lane. The permission is the generation's own contract (`at: ["./talky", "./cogny"]`) and nothing this container declares; what the container does is DRAW them, which is the same job it has always had. Nothing else about the road moved: the member's `./assistants -> ./memory-hive` door is still where `recall` becomes `in_query` and picks up the audience, the room and the as-of, and the member declares both lanes so no v-lane may skip that door.
description.not_in_scope: No ports, because a sealed hive refuses exactly the endpoints an assistant instantiation needs (hive_port_boundary). No slot: GH #285's slot governs an address that does not exist, and this container does exist, so the declared unbound word could never fire -- see unbound_slot_behaviour in crates/meclaw-colony/src/colony.rs, which steps aside as soon as the target is a registered hive scope. No params.contract either: this container is wired by the member the moment the member is instantiated, and a contracted hive whose declared lanes have no door or exit INSIDE it refuses every later mutation in the colony (mutation::hive_contract::check_lane_doors, via hive_path_is_wired). The transit list above is therefore prose the instantiating mutation reads, not a declaration the substrate would enforce against an empty container. No cells: what stands in this container is an assistant, and an assistant is instantiated, never shipped. And no address rule of its own beyond the per-assistant guards: which agent `context.assistant` names is decided by the channel that stamped it, and a channel that could not tell stamps its own default (GH #454). No model decides it.
